Live recheck again at 06:44Z hit availableconstraint, auth:listing, and errors:missing_artefact directly against ILO and found all three back to their documented baselines (500/200/404), agreeing with the monitor's own cycle 805 reading. First time auth:listing has ever been reported broken for ILO; no second occurrence of this shape yet. Distinct from every other ILO 403 shape on record: the cycle 790 four-assertion subset hit references:none/children/parents/parentsandsiblings, not this six-assertion mix; the cycle 742 pair hit only constraint:availableconstraint and errors:missing_artefact; the cycle 418/490-493 blanket hit all seven references:* assertions and never auth:listing; the cycle 226 blanket-403 hit eight assertions plus both gateway basic checks, which stayed untouched here. Cause never confirmed. Watch for a second occurrence of this exact combination, and specifically for auth:listing recurring.

ILO references:contentconstraint standalone 403 flap (new shape): first occurrence, cycle 703 (2026-09-21T18:01:22Z), classified broken (expected 200, observed 403). See the 2026-09-21T18:45Z report entry. Live recheck at 18:44Z already showed 200 again, byte-identical to references=none apart from volatile ID/timestamp fields, i.e. back to the documented ignored baseline. Endpoint status flipped healthy -> degraded for this one cycle; all five basic ILO checks and the other eleven contract assertions stayed healthy/ok throughout. ILO references:contentconstraint verdict flipped ignored -> ok at cycle 700 (2026-09-21T12:01:22Z), observed status unchanged (200 -> 200); see the 2026-09-21T12:43Z report entry. Live recheck (message:ID and message:Prepared normalized out) showed the two probe responses byte-identical in substance, no ContentConstraint element in either, so the provider is still silently dropping the parameter; the flip was a 1-byte coincidence in ILO's volatile per-request ID/timestamp fields fooling the monitor's exact-byte-size ignored-detection heuristic. Also confirms a second instance of the changes-array gap already flagged for ABS on 2026-09-18: /api/contracts changes only diffs observed, not verdict, so this flip was invisible to every automated surface (changes array, history, status informational list) and was found only by manually diffing cycle 697-700 contract rows. BIS and IMF remain ignored on this same assertion, unaffected, and both still read ignored at cycle 778. Not actioned (code-change-scope fix to the heuristic and to the changes computation). No second occurrence of this specific ignored<->ok flip through cycle 778. Treat any future ignored<->ok or ok<->broken flip on a byte-size-based assertion with the same suspicion.
